sources.text: 28-120.1 § 28-120.1 Tenant protection plan. A tenant protection plan shall be prepared and submitted for the alteration, construction, or partial demolition of buildings in which any dwelling unit will be occupied during construction, including newly constructed buildings that are partially occupied where work is ongoing. The tenant protection plan shall be prepared by a registered design professional and filed with the department. The registered design professional preparing the tenant protection plan shall be retained by the general contractor performing the alteration, construction, or partial demolition work. No permit shall be issued for work that requires a tenant protection plan unless such plan is approved by the department. Such plan shall contain a statement signed by the owner and signed by the applicant affirming that the building contains dwelling units that will be occupied during construction and shall identify in sufficient detail the specific units that are or may be occupied during construction, the means and methods to be employed to safeguard the safety and health of the occupants throughout the construction, including, where applicable, details such as temporary fire-rated assemblies, opening protectives, or dust containment procedures. Such means and methods shall be described with particularity and in no case shall terms such as "code compliant," "approved," "legal," "protected in accordance with law" or similar terms be used as a substitute for such description. The tenant protection plan must be site specific. The elements of the tenant protection plan may vary depending on the nature and scope of the work but at a minimum, must comply with all applicable laws and regulations, including the New York city construction codes, the New York city housing maintenance code, the New York city noise control code and the New York city health code, and shall make detailed and specific provisions for: 1. Egress. At all times in the course of construction provision shall be made for adequate egress as required by this code and the tenant protection plan shall identify the egress that will be provided. Required egress shall not be obstructed at any time except where approved by the commissioner. 2. Fire safety. All necessary laws and controls, including those with respect to occupied dwellings, as well as additional safety measures necessitated by the construction shall be strictly observed. 3. Health requirements. Specification of means and methods to be used for control of dust, disposal of construction debris, pest control and maintenance of sanitary facilities shall be included. 3.1. Lead and asbestos. Where the work involves disturbance of lead-based paint, as defined in section 27-2056.2 , or paint of unknown lead content or asbestos, there shall be included a statement of compliance with applicable provisions of law relating to lead and asbestos, including whether the firm performing proposed work holds the certification or certifications required to perform such work pursuant to section 27-2056.11 , and disclosure of any open violations related to lead issued by the department of health and mental hygiene or the department of housing preservation and development. 4. Compliance with housing standards. The requirements of the New York city housing maintenance code, and, where applicable, the New York state multiple dwelling law shall be strictly observed. 5. Structural safety. No structural work shall be done that may endanger the occupants. 6. Noise restrictions. Specification of means and methods to be used for the limitation of noise to acceptable levels in accordance with the New York city noise control code shall be included. Where hours of the day or the days of the week in which construction work may be undertaken are limited pursuant to the New York city noise control code, such limitations shall be stated. 7. Maintaining essential services. Where heat, hot water, cold water, gas, electricity, or other utility services are provided in such building or in any dwelling unit located therein, the tenant protection plan shall specify the means and methods to be used for maintaining such services during such work in accordance with the requirements of the New York city housing maintenance code. If a disruption of any such service is anticipated during the work, then such plan shall specify the anticipated duration of such disruption and the means and methods to be employed to minimize such disruption, including the provision of sufficient alternatives for such service during such disruption. Notification of the disruption must be given to all affected occupants of occupied dwelling units. Exception: In the following instances, the tenant protection plan may be prepared and filed by the regist

28-103.27 § 28-103.27 Disclosure of building occupancy status for buildings subject to permit. For each building for which a permit for work has been issued, the commissioner shall post on the department's website a statement of whether the construction documents relating to such permit indicate that one or more dwelling units within such building will be occupied during such work. (L.L. 2017/158, 8/30/2017, eff. 8/30/2018)

28-105.11 § 28-105.11 Posting of permit. The building permit or copy shall be posted in a conspicuous place at the work site, visible to the public for the duration of the work or the use and operation of the equipment, or until the expiration of the permit. No such permit shall be posted or displayed at any location other than the location of the premises or equipment for which the permit was issued. Where the permit is exposed to the weather, it shall be laminated or encased in a plastic covering to protect it from the elements. The permit shall identify whether any dwelling unit within such building will be occupied during the work. If dwelling units within such building will be occupied during the work, the permit shall indicate the total number of dwelling units that will be occupied. Exception: Where a project information panel is required by section 3301.9.1 of the New York city building code, the permit shall be posted in accordance with such section, and no other permits shall be posted in any location readily visible to the public, except as provided in section 3301.9.5 of the New York city building code. (Am. L.L. 2017/158, 8/30/2017, eff. 8/30/2018)

28-105.5.2 § 28-105.5.2 Application for permit where a building is occupied. All applications for permits for work on a building having more than three dwelling units shall state (i) the total number of units in the building at the time the application is filed, (ii) the number of units occupied at the time the application is filed, and (iii) the number of units to be occupied during the course of the work. The work permit application shall be amended prior to occupancy of any units that were not initially counted as being occupied during the course of the work. (L.L. 2017/149, 8/30/2017, eff. 12/28/2017; Am. L.L. 2021/126, 11/7/2021, eff. 11/7/2022) Editor's note: For related unconsolidated provisions, see Appendix A at L.L. 2021/126 .

28-103.30.2 § 28-103.30.2 Monitoring occupied multiple dwellings with permits for alteration or addition. The real time enforcement unit shall monitor all occupied multiple dwellings with valid permits for (i) the alteration of 10 percent or more of the existing floor surface area of the building or (ii) an addition to the building. Owners of such buildings shall notify the department in writing at least 72 hours prior to the commencement of any work pursuant to such permits. (L.L. 2017/188, 10/16/2017, eff. 2/13/2018; Am. L.L. 2017/233, 12/1/2017, eff. 12/1/2018)

28-105.1.5 § 28-105.1.5 Denial of permits for work without permit on occupied building. The commissioner shall not issue a permit for a building for at least one year following the date of a determination by the commissioner that work has been performed without a permit in such building and such building was occupied at the time such work was being performed. Such denial shall not apply where a dwelling unit within such multiple dwelling is owned as a condominium or held by a shareholder of a cooperative corporation under a proprietary lease. Exceptions: 1. Where the issuance of such permit is necessary to correct an outstanding violation of this code, the New York city housing maintenance code or any other applicable provisions of law or rule. 2. Where the issuance of such permit is necessary to perform work to protect public health and safety. 3. For a portion of a property occupied by a tenant who is not an owner of such property or responsible for any existing violations in such property. 4. Where a property was the subject of an in rem foreclosure judgment in favor of the city and was transferred by the city to a third party pursuant to section 11-412.1 of the administrative code. 5. Where a property is the subject of a court order appointing an administrator pursuant to article 7-A of the New York state real property actions and proceedings law in a case brought by the department of housing preservation and development. 6. Where a property is the subject of a loan provided by or through the department of housing preservation and development or the New York city housing development corporation for the purpose of rehabilitation that has closed within the five years preceding the application for such permit. 7. For a property where the department of housing preservation and development or the New York city housing development corporation notifies the commissioner that the permit is required in connection with the implementation of a program of such department or corporation. (L.L. 2019/114, 6/8/2019, eff. 12/5/2019; Am. L.L. 2021/126, 11/7/2021, eff. 11/7/2022) Editor's note: For related unconsolidated provisions, see Appendix A at L.L. 2021/126 .

28-105.1.4 § 28-105.1.4 Denial of permits for false statements on applications for construction document approval. The commissioner shall not issue a permit for an occupied building for at least one year following the date of a determination by the commissioner that a false statement about the occupancy status of such building has been made in an application for construction document approval. Such denial shall not apply where a dwelling unit within such multiple dwelling is owned as a condominium or held by a shareholder of a cooperative corporation under a proprietary lease. Exceptions: 1. Where the issuance of such permit is necessary to correct an outstanding violation of this code, the New York city housing maintenance code or any other applicable provisions of law or rule. 2. Where the issuance of such permit is necessary to perform work to protect public health and safety. 3. For a portion of a property occupied by a tenant who is not an owner of such property or responsible for any existing violations in such property. 4. Where a property was the subject of an in rem foreclosure judgment in favor of the city and was transferred by the city to a third party pursuant to section 11-412.1 of the administrative code. 5. Where a property is the subject of a court order appointing an administrator pursuant to article 7-A of the New York state real property actions and proceedings law in a case brought by the department of housing preservation and development. 6. Where a property is the subject of a loan provided by or through the department of housing preservation and development or the New York city housing development corporation for the purpose of rehabilitation that has closed within the five years preceding the application for such permit. 7. For a property where the department of housing preservation and development or the New York city housing development corporation notifies the commissioner that the permit is required in connection with the implementation of a program of such department or corporation. (L.L. 2019/114, 6/8/2019, eff. 12/5/2019; Am. L.L. 2021/126, 11/7/2021, eff. 11/7/2022) Editor's note: For related unconsolidated provisions, see Appendix A at L.L. 2021/126 .

28-103.30 § 28-103.30 Real time enforcement unit. There is hereby established within the department a real time enforcement unit. Such unit and an agency that is delegated authority by the commissioner shall be responsible for enforcing the construction codes with respect to: 1. occupied multiple dwellings with complaints related to work without a permit; and 2. occupied multiple dwellings with valid permits for (i) the alteration of 10 percent or more of the existing floor surface area of the building or (ii) an addition to the building. (L.L. 2017/188, 10/16/2017, eff. 2/13/2018; Am. L.L; Am. L.L. 2017/233, 12/1/2017, eff. 12/1/2018)

310.4 310.4 Residential Group R-2. Residential Group R-2 occupancies shall include buildings or portions thereof containing sleeping units or more than two dwelling units that are occupied for permanent residence purposes as defined in subparagraph (a) of paragraph 8 of subdivision a of Section 27-2004 of the New York City Housing Maintenance Code . Such occupancy shall be subject to the New York State Multiple Dwelling Law . This group shall include, but not be limited to, the following: Adult homes or enriched housing with 16 or fewer occupants requiring supervised care on a 24-hour basis in the same building, provided that the number of occupants per dwelling unit does not exceed the definition of a family Apartment houses Apartment hotels (nontransient) Class A multiple dwellings as defined in Section 27-2004 of the New York City Housing Maintenance Code and Section 4 of the New York State Multiple Dwelling Law , where not classified in Group I, including the following: 1. Dwelling units where the resident of the unit provides custodial care to no more than four persons on less than a 24-hour basis and not overnight, where not classified in Group I. 2. Dwelling units where the resident of the unit provides child custodial care as a family day care home registered with the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene in accordance with the New York State Social Services Law , with no more than six children between the ages of 2 and 13, or with no more than five children if any are under the age of 2, receiving supervised care on less than a 24-hour basis and not overnight, where not classified in Group I. Convents and monasteries with more than 20 occupants in the building Student apartments (Am. L.L. 2023/077, 6/11/2023, eff. 6/11/2023) Editor's note: For related unconsolidated provisions, see Appendix A at L.L. 2023/077 .

28-120.3 § 28-120.3 Contractor statement. The permit holder for the underlying alteration, construction, or partial demolition shall sign a statement certifying that the tenant protection plan submitted by the registered design professional coordinates with the scope of work intended. Exception: This statement shall not be required for: 1. Work in occupied one- and two-family homes. 2. Work limited to the interior of a single dwelling unit of an occupied multiple dwelling with no disruption to the essential services of other units, where such dwelling is owner-occupied. For a dwelling unit within a property that is owned by a condominium or held by a shareholder of a cooperative corporation under a proprietary lease, the unit must be occupied by the owners of record for such unit. (L.L. 2019/106, 6/8/2019, eff. 3/8/2020)

retrieval.webQuery: Context: DOB NOW workflow At least one residential unit will be occupied during construction at some point before the permit is signed off by DOB. How should the occupied-dwelling-unit question be answered, and what follows?

answer.disclaimer: AI-generated research assistance—not an official code determination. Verify cited text, source status, and Project facts before relying on this answer for filing, design, permitting, or construction.

content.text:
- **Alteration required to meet New Building requirements? — No.** The stated scope does not require compliance as a New Building; “Yes” would route to **Alteration CO – New Building with Existing Elements to Remain**. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))
- **Alteration is inconsistent with the current Certificate of Occupancy? — No.** The proposed work is consistent with the current Certificate of Occupancy; “Yes” would route to **Alteration CO**. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))
- **Alteration in occupancy or use? — No.** The stated scope does not change occupancy or use; “Yes” would route to **Alteration CO**. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))
- **Alteration is a major change to exits? — No.** The stated scope does not change the exits in a major way; “Yes” would route to **Alteration CO**. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))
- **Alteration in number of stories? — No.** The stated scope does not change the number of stories; the guide identifies “Yes” as producing **Alteration CO** for Building Type “3 Family” or “Other.” ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))
- **Resulting job type: Alteration (Alt), not Alteration CO.** DOB’s guide states that when all five Alteration-routing questions are answered “No,” the filing is an **Alteration** and does not require an amended Certificate of Occupancy. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))

{"paragraphs":[{"text":"Answer “No” to each of the five Alteration-routing questions: (1) alteration required to meet New Building requirements; (2) alteration inconsistent with the current Certificate of Occupancy; (3) alteration in occupancy or use; (4) alteration a major change to exits; and (5) alteration in number of stories. On the stated facts, the resulting DOB NOW job type is “Alteration” (not requiring an amended Certificate of Occupancy). This is the User Guide’s routing workflow; it does not itself establish code compliance or approve the filing.","sourceUses":[{"sourceID":"web-source-eff9cc5f5b0cfde883cce536","claimID":"official-passage-5b682c1399f57019c03eda89"}]},{"text":"The guide states that a “Yes” to the New Building-requirements question routes the filing to “Alteration CO – New Building with Existing Elements to Remain”; a “Yes” to the Certificate of Occupancy, occupancy/use, or major-exits question routes it to “Alteration CO.” A “Yes” to the stories question does so only where the Building Type is “3 Family or Other.” Because all five stated answers are No, that building-type qualification does not affect this result.","sourceUses":[{"sourceID":"web-source-eff9cc5f5b0cfde883cce536","claimID":"official-passage-5b682c1399f57019c03eda89"}]},{"text":"These five job-type selections are made when the job is created and cannot be changed later in the indicated DOB NOW section.","sourceUses":[{"sourceID":"web-source-eff9cc5f5b0cfde883cce536","claimID":"official-passage-5bdd162d6e75ae930ee42abc"}]}],"missingFacts":[],"evidenceLimitations":[]}

- **No.** DOB’s August 2026 release notes state that LPC-calendared properties receive an automatic **40-day hold** before the filing can be approved; for a Standard Plan Examination filing, the hold begins when the job reaches **PE Review**. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_build_release_notes.pdf))

- DOB also states that it **will not issue a permit for work on a landmarked property without LPC approval**, including Initial Alteration filings, except for specified exempt work types. The release notes identify an LPC Approval/Permit document and Landmark Fee treatment as filing requirements. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_build_release_notes.pdf))

- The DOB NOW Application User Guide states that LPC approval is required for applicable landmark-related work and that **LPC-approved drawings must be submitted before filing**; it also says the Landmark selection may be auto-populated from the property profile. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))

- The supplied LPC landing page identifies LPC resources, including the Permit Guidebook and permit-application tools, but it does **not itself establish a substantive minimum approval rule** for this DOB workflow. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/site/lpc/index.page))

- Accordingly, based on these official workflow materials, the Researcher should **not promise immediate DOB approval without LPC processing**. This is administrative workflow context, not a project-specific compliance determination.

- **The property address alone is not enough to choose a Building Code review year in DOB NOW.** The application guide instructs the applicant to select the code under which the review is requested and states that the available choice depends on the **job type, filing date, and work type**. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))

- **The correct researcher response is to request the missing filing facts—not to infer a code year from the building address.** At minimum, identify the proposed job type, work type, filing date, and any applicable related or prior job information. This is an administrative workflow answer, not a project compliance determination. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))

- **For electrical filings, DOB’s August 2025 release notes show that the dropdown is conditional:** reinstatements of BIS electrical filings present “Prior to 2008/2011,” “2008 NEC/2011 NYC Electrical Code,” and “2020 NEC/2025 NYC Electrical Code,” while filings with a related BIS/DOB NOW job present the latter two options. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_build_release_notes.pdf))

- **Therefore, do not answer “select [year]” solely from an address.** State that the address may identify the property record, but it does not by itself establish the applicable DOB NOW Code Review Year; the filing context and the governing enacted code provisions must be researched before selecting an option. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))

- For work that is part of the **same construction project and property**, DOB NOW guidance states that all related filings should use the **same job number**, with an extension identifying the filing as Initial, Subsequent, or Post Approval Amendment. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))
- The plumbing scope should therefore generally be filed as a **Subsequent (S) filing under the existing job number**, rather than as a new unrelated job. A subsequent filing may be created by the original applicant or a **new applicant** and may add new scope and work types. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))
- Plumbing is a recognized DOB NOW work type, covering specified installation, maintenance, repair, modification, extension, or alteration work. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))
- To create it, use **Search** in DOB NOW: Build, locate the initial filing by BIN or job number, and select **Subsequent Filing** from the Filing Action column. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))
- The subsequent filing functions as a separate application for permitting and Letter of Completion purposes, even though it remains under the same job number. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))

{"paragraphs":[{"text":"The plumbing scope should be filed as a subsequent filing under the existing job number, rather than as a new unrelated job number, if it is part of the same construction project. DOB NOW guidance says that all filings for the same construction project should use the same job number with an alphabetic/numeric extension; a subsequent filing adds new scope of work and new work types on the same property.","sourceUses":[{"sourceID":"web-source-eff9cc5f5b0cfde883cce536","claimID":"official-passage-789cc7ccd439eb8374132031"}]},{"text":"A subsequent filing may be submitted by a new applicant rather than the applicant on the initial GC filing. If the plumbing work is instead only a qualifying repair or replacement of existing equipment with no construction work, the guide describes a separate Limited Alteration plumbing application category; the provided passages do not resolve whether that circumstance changes the related-filing approach for this project.","sourceUses":[{"sourceID":"web-source-eff9cc5f5b0cfde883cce536","claimID":"official-passage-674fa7301b0f8839e37fe829"}]}],"missingFacts":[],"evidenceLimitations":["The supplied passages do not state whether a Limited Alteration plumbing application that qualifies under its specific no-construction-work description must or may be linked as a subsequent filing to an existing GC project job."]}

- **Filing action:** Submit a **Post Approval Amendment (PAA)** because the approved filing, scope, or drawings are being changed after approval. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))

- **Legalization limitation:** Because the filing was **not submitted as a legalization**, do not select Legalization for this revision. DOB’s guide states that legalization filings result in a **no-work permit** and that **PAAs are not allowed** once Legalization is selected. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))

- **Limits to disclose:** The PAA should identify the approved work being revised and clearly describe the changes to the scope and drawings. The supplied official pages establish the PAA mechanism and the prohibition on PAAs for legalization filings, but they do **not** state a broader numeric or substantive limit on the permissible extent of revisions. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))

- **No.** DOB NOW’s user guide says to answer **“Yes”** only when the application relates to a project **enrolled in** the Major Projects Development Program (MPP). A project’s size or cost alone does not establish enrollment. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))
- The DOB release notes describe MPP as a voluntary program and state that the enrollment fee is due **upon MPP acceptance by the Department**. Because the project has not been accepted, it should not be identified as an approved MPP project. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_build_release_notes.pdf))
- The user guide is administrative guidance and expressly states that it does not supersede the Building Code, Zoning Resolution, or other applicable rules, regulations, or policies. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))

- Selecting **“Yes”** causes an **FDNY Letter of No Objection** to be required before approval. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))

- The DOB NOW guide describes plumbing work as including, among other work, sprinkler work supplied from the domestic water service. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))

{"paragraphs":[{"text":"Answer “Yes” to the plumbing question, “Does the PL work impact the water supply to the Sprinkler and/or Standpipe system?” On the stated facts, the plumbing work will interrupt or otherwise affect that water supply. - The DOB NOW Application User Guide states that the stormwater questions apply to **New Building, Alteration-CO, and Alterations with Enlargement** filings. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))
- The condition is triggered by either **soil disturbance of 20,000 square feet or more** or **creation of 5,000 square feet or more of impervious surface**. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))
- On the stated facts, the **19,000-square-foot soil disturbance alone is below the threshold**, but the **exactly 5,000 square feet of impervious surface meets the “5,000 square feet or more” threshold**. Thus, the stated DOB NOW condition applies, subject to the guide’s separate “larger common plan or development or sale” question. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))
- If either applicable DOB NOW question is answered “Yes,” the guide identifies a **DEP Stormwater Construction Permit** as required before approval and a **DEP Stormwater Maintenance Permit/Notice of Termination** as required before sign-off. This is workflow guidance, not a project-specific compliance determination or a substitute for the enacted legal authority. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))

For an otherwise applicable New Building, Alteration-CO, or Alteration-with-Enlargement filing, the stated stormwater condition applies because the work creates exactly 5,000 square feet of impervious surface, meeting the “5,000 square feet or more” threshold. - Answer **“Yes”** to the DOB NOW question about whether dwelling units will be occupied during construction. DOB’s guide states that a **Tenant Protection Plan (TPP) is required if any residential unit will be occupied at any time before the permit is signed off by DOB**. - Because the answer is **Yes**, DOB NOW requires a **Tenant Protection Plan** for the filing. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))

- The subsequent occupied-unit questions determine which tenant-protection-law compliance requirements apply, including whether residential units are occupied **at the time of application**. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))

- DOB’s guide separately states that, where a TPP is required, answering **Yes** to Questions 8, 9, or 10 means a **Tenant Protection Plan Compliance special inspection will not be required**.
